arxiv-2104-00863.title: PolyDNN Polynomial Representation of NN for Communication-less SMPC Inference
arxiv-2104-00863.creator: Philip Derbeko and Shlomi Dolev
arxiv-2104-00863.description: Abstract The structure and weights of Deep Neural Networks (DNN) typically encode and contain very valuable information about the dataset that was used to train the network. One way to protect this information when DNN is published is to perform an interference of the network using secure multi-party computations (MPC).

arxiv-2106-07213.title: TweetPap: A Dataset to Study the Social Media Discourse of Scientific Papers
arxiv-2106-07213.creator: Naman Jain and Mayank Singh
arxiv-2106-07213.description: Abstract Nowadays, researchers have moved to platforms like Twitter to spread information about their ideas and empirical evidence. Recent studies have shown that social media affects the scientific impact of a paper. However, these studies only utilize the tweet counts to represent Twitter activity.

arxiv-2110-12001.title: Brownian Motion & The Stochastic Behaviour of Stocks
arxiv-2110-12001.creator: Yorgos Protonotarios, Pantelis Tassopoulos
arxiv-2110-12001.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yorgos Protonotarios, Pantelis Tassopoulos. 1 Introduction 1.1 Robert Brown In 1827, a botanist by the name of Robert Brown was examining the motion of grains of pollen suspended under water from a species of plants. Brown observed the motion of the particles ejected from these pollen grains which followed a seemingly ”jittery” motion; this was the first ever recorded case of Brownian motion, named after Robert Brown.

arxiv-2210-10884.title: Inference finds consistency between a neutrino flavor evolution model and Earth-based solar neutrino measurements Preprint: N3AS-22-022, SLAC-PUB-17705
arxiv-2210-10884.creator: Caroline Laber-Smith, A.A. Ahmetaj, Eve Armstrong, A. Baha Balantekin, Amol V. Patwardhan, M. Margarette Sanchez, Sherry Wong
arxiv-2210-10884.description: Abstract We continue examining statistical data assimilation (SDA), an inference methodology, to infer solutions to neutrino flavor evolution, for the first time using real – rather than simulated – data. The model represents neutrinos streaming from the Sun’s center and undergoing a Mikheyev-Smirnov-Wolfenstein (MSW) resonance in flavor space, due to the radially-varying electron number density.

arxiv-2309-13820.title: Strongly Efficient Rare-Event Simulation for Regularly Varying Lévy Processes with Infinite Activities
arxiv-2309-13820.creator: Xingyu Wang, Chang-Han Rhee
arxiv-2309-13820.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xingyu Wang, Chang-Han Rhee. In this paper, we address rare-event simulation for heavy-tailed Lévy processes with infinite activities. The presence of infinite activities poses a critical challenge, making it impractical to simulate or store the precise sample path of the Lévy process. We present a rare-event simulation algorithm that incorporates an importance sampling strategy based on heavy-tailed large deviations, the stick-breaking approximation for the extrema of Lévy processes, the Asmussen-Rosiński approximation, and the randomized debiasing technique.

arxiv-2310-07302.title: Schanuel’s lemma for extriangulated categories
arxiv-2310-07302.creator: Hangyu Yin
arxiv-2310-07302.description:
A 2023 arXiv research paper by Hangyu Yin. In the context of extriangulated categories, we establish the injective version of Schanuel’s lemma in homological algebra. Keywords : extriangulated category; homological algebra; injective dimension 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification: 18G80; 18E10



1
Introduction

In the realm of mathematics, specifically within the field of algebra, particularly module theory, Schanuel’s lemma, attributed to Stephen Schanuel, offers a means to assess the extent to which modules deviate from being projective.

arxiv-2504-11238.title: Probe of Generic Quantum Contextuality and Nonlocal Resources for Qubits
arxiv-2504-11238.creator: Wei Li, Min-Xuan Zhou, Yun-Hao Shi, Z. D. Wang, Heng Fan, Yan-Kui Bai
arxiv-2504-11238.description: Abstract We reveal that the entropic uncertainty relation with a quantum memory is able to intrinsically connect local generic contextuality addressed in the pioneering work by Spekkens [ 1 ] and nonlocal quantum resources such as entanglement and Bell nonlocality.

arxiv-2505-08707.title: Universal electronic synthesis by microresonator-soliton photomixing
arxiv-2505-08707.creator: Jizhao Zang, Travis C. Briles, Jesse S. Morgan, Andreas Beling, Scott B. Papp
arxiv-2505-08707.description: Abstract Access to electrical signals across the millimeter-wave (mmW) and terahertz (THz) bands offers breakthroughs for high-performance applications. Despite generations of revolutionary development, integrated electronics are challenging to operate beyond 100 GHz. Therefore, new technologies that generate wideband and tunable electronic signals would advance wireless communication, high-resolution imaging and scanning, spectroscopy, and network formation.

arxiv-2508-13900.title: A general search for supersymmetric particles in scenarios with compressed mass spectra using proton-proton collisions at s = 13 ​ \TeV \sqrt{s}=13\TeV
arxiv-2508-13900.description: Abstract A general search is presented for supersymmetric particles (sparticles) in scenarios featuring compressed mass spectra using proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 \TeV , recorded with the CMS detector at the LHC. The analyzed data sample corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 138 \fbinv .

arxiv-2511-13605.title: Chasing Submodular Objectives, and Submodular Maximization via Cutting Planes
arxiv-2511-13605.creator: Niv Buchbinder, Joseph (Seffi) Naor, David Wajc
arxiv-2511-13605.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Niv Buchbinder, Joseph (Seffi) Naor, David Wajc. We introduce the submodular objectives chasing problem , which generalizes many natural and previously-studied problems: a sequence of constrained submodular maximization problems is revealed over time, with both the objective and available ground set changing at each step. The goal is to maintain solutions of high approximation and low total recourse (number of changes), compared with exact offline algorithms for the same input sequence.

arxiv-2602-18773.title: LAMMI-Pathology: A Tool-Centric Bottom-Up LVLM-Agent Framework for Molecularly Informed Medical Intelligence in Pathology
arxiv-2602-18773.creator: Haoyang Su, Shaoting Zhang, Xiaosong Wang
arxiv-2602-18773.description: Abstract The emergence of tool-calling-based agent systems introduces a more evidence-driven paradigm for pathology image analysis in contrast to the coarse-grained text-image diagnostic approaches. With the recent large-scale experimental adoption of spatial transcriptomics technologies, molecularly validated pathological diagnosis is becoming increasingly open and accessible.

pmc-10613352.title: Changes in work tasks and organization of general practice in Norway during the COVID-19 pandemic: results from a comparative international study
pmc-10613352.creator: Torunn Bjerve Eide, Esther van Poel, Sara Willems, Frode F Jacobsen
pmc-10613352.description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic led to huge and rapid changes in general practice in Norway as in the rest of Europe. This paper aims to explore to what extent the COVID-19 pandemic changed the work tasks and organization of Norwegian general practice.

pmc-11435395.title: Comparative Analysis of Phytohormone Biosynthesis Genes Responses to Long-Term High Light in Tolerant and Sensitive Wheat Cultivars
pmc-11435395.creator: Zhi-Ang Li, Muhammad Fahad, Wan-Chang Li, Leeza Tariq, Miao-Miao Liu, Ya-Nan Liu, Tai-Xia Wang, Vladimir V Kuznetsov
pmc-11435395.description: Phytohormones are vital for developmental processes, from organ initiation to senescence, and are key regulators of growth, development, and photosynthesis. In natural environments, plants often experience high light (HL) intensities coupled with elevated temperatures, which pose significant threats to agricultural production. However, the response of phytohormone-related genes to long-term HL exposure remains unclear.

pmc-11532472.title: The emotional effect of terrorism
pmc-11532472.creator: Vincenzo Bove, Georgios Efthyvoulou, Armine Ghazaryan, Harry Pickard
pmc-11532472.description: Terrorism causes emotional reactions among public audiences, with downstream consequences for their well-being, attitudes and policy preferences. We utilise a novel approach which harnesses a unique dataset of Twitter activity from 324K users to precisely capture emotional responses to terrorism.

pmc-12434401.title: Navigating change: the role of change management strategies and cultural factors in Saudi Arabian organizations
pmc-12434401.creator: Chiraz Mohamed Rouissi
pmc-12434401.description: BackgroundOrganizational change remains a critical challenge in the industrial sectors of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, where leadership practices and deep-rooted cultural norms significantly influence transformation efforts. Despite a growing body of global change management literature, limited empirical research addresses the interplay between cultural dynamics and change management within the Saudi context.

pmc-12749691.title: HPV16-miR-H1 promotes proliferation, migration, and glycolysis in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma cells via the PTEN/AKT pathway
pmc-12749691.creator: Ruilin Wang, Shangdong Li, Yuxiu Ma, Dezhuan Da, Qi Zhang, Chunyan Dang, Xuhui Zhao, Shuang Liang, Hongling Li
pmc-12749691.description: Human papillomavirus type 16 (HPV16) is the most common type of infection in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC).The HPV16-encoded miRNA, HPV16-miR-H1, has been validated in cervical cancer tissues and cells, but its role in the pathogenesis of HNSCC remains unclear.
